what: Flight statement of the Fury model (estimates)
statement: Assumptions of the flight statement. None is manufacturer data.

weights.structure_note: modelled structure 1136 lb (analysis/results/mass.json, measured on the model) x 1.30 allowance
weights.engine_note: engine and jet pipe as in analysis/results/mass.json (engine weight assumed there from the public FJ44-4 figure)
weights.fuel_note: what the modelled fuel cells hold (749 US gal); the real fuel load is not published
weights.stores_note: two AIM-120-class missiles on pylon launchers, as in the photographs the model was matched to

light.label: 5,000 lb: the gross weight published for the original Fury design

weights.inertia_note: radii of gyration of a single-engine jet fighter (Raymer table 16.1: 0.23, 0.38, 0.52 of half span, half length and their mean); Ixz 5 % of Ixx (ASSUMPTION)
weights.statement: ESTIMATE. The real weights are not published. The one public figure, 5,000 lb gross weight, was given for the original, smaller Fury design; it is carried as the "light" case.

engine.name: Williams FJ44-4M
engine.source: Thrust 3,790 lbf sea-level static: public figure of the FJ44-4M (Aero L-39NG data); the FJ44-4M is the engine publicly named for the YFQ-44A. Lapse with speed and height: Mattingly, Heiser and Pratt high-bypass form with the Mach term reduced to 0.30 for a bypass ratio of 3 to 4 (ASSUMPTION), flat rated to a throttle ratio of 1.04. Installation: (1 - 1.35 x (1 - recovery)) x offtake x nozzle = 0.926 with an assumed inlet recovery of 0.97. No afterburner. Uncertainty about plus or minus 15 % at speed and height.

neutral_point.note: Two estimates. Used in the flight model: lattice of wing and tail plus the fuselage moment by the Multhopp strip method. The flow solution of the whole aircraft (four angles, one grid) puts the neutral point further forward, and it moves aft with angle of attack. The flight model assumes a static margin, not a place: the centre of gravity is set a fixed fraction of the mean chord ahead of the estimate used, so with the flow-solution value the same flight behaviour needs the centre of gravity that much further forward.

balance.cg_rule: ASSUMPTION: 5 % of the mean chord ahead of the estimated neutral point, the same for every weight case
balance.open_point: The items of the weight model (structure, engine, gear, fuel; no systems) balance at station 19.5 ft with full fuel and the main wheels stand at 19.8 ft, both well aft of the flight centre of gravity assumed here (17.9 ft). Flown at the modelled balance the aircraft would be 18 % of the mean chord unstable against the estimated neutral point. Either the real neutral point is further aft than this shape gives, or the real mass is further forward, or the real aircraft flies unstable on its flight control system. Not resolved.

drag.source: Zero-lift drag: equivalent skin friction 0.0030 on the wetted area of the model (830 ft2, measured). Drag due to lift: 1 / (pi AR) with a leading-edge suction schedule, the rest of the lift force tilted back by the angle of attack. Compressibility: Korn equation with Lock's fourth-power rise. Stores, gear, flap: drag areas and the plain-flap profile drag rule as stated in ASSUME. The flow solution is not used for drag; it gives less zero-lift drag (0.0099 against 0.0173) and about twice the drag due to lift (CD = CD0 + 0.20 CL2 against about 0.09 CL2 here), see the sensitivity in turn.md.

lift.note: Lift slope from the lattice (wing and tail carried to the centreline). The flow solution gives a lower slope (3.52 against 4.27 per rad at low speed): if it is right, every angle of attack quoted for a given lift is about 21 % too small. Lift and pitching moment at zero angle of attack are taken from the flow solution.

earlier_runs.note: Void: wrongly turned triangles in the flow-body mesh made the solver treat air behind the wing trailing edge as solid.
